criteria_results.title: Case caption includes correct case number
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption includes the case number exactly as required: 1:25-cv-01043-RWS.

criteria_results.title: Case caption identifies correct court
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption states “IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT,” “FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF GEORGIA,” and “ATLANTA DIVISION,” which matches the required court identification.

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies Meridian Supply Chain Solutions, Inc. as Plaintiff
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption names “MERIDIAN SUPPLY CHAIN SOLUTIONS, INC.” and labels it as Plaintiff.

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies Caldwell Industrial Technologies, LLC as Defendant
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption lists “CALDWELL INDUSTRIAL TECHNOLOGIES, LLC, a Georgia limited liability company” and labels it as “Defendant,” satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Answer responds to every numbered paragraph of the Complaint
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer provides individual paragraph-by-paragraph responses to the Complaint’s numbered allegations, including paragraphs 1 through 91, with admissions, denials, partial admissions/denials, and lack-of-knowledge responses. This far exceeds the threshold of at least 50 numbered paragraph responses.

criteria_results.title: Acknowledges Tranche 1 rejection was sent by email rather than formal notice method
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly acknowledges that the September 27, 2024 Tranche 1 rejection notice was transmitted by email, addresses MSA Section 19.1, and argues that the written email notice was effective because it was actually received and acted upon. It also discusses this issue in the affirmative defenses.

criteria_results.title: Asserts Meridian waived formal notice requirement through substantive response
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly asserts waiver/estoppel based on Meridian’s substantive response to the September 27 email rejection, including Kyle Densmore’s acknowledgment of receipt, review of the QC materials, escalation/investigation, proposal of joint inspection, and failure to object to the email form until months later. It does not admit the rejection was defective without asserting waiver.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Asserts force majeure as an affirmative defense
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer lists a specific “TENTH DEFENSE (Force Majeure)” invoking MSA Section 12.1. It references the Tidewater project suspension/directive barring further deliveries and states Caldwell gave timely written notice. The Answer also expressly alleges the October 2, 2024 Tidewater suspension and Caldwell’s October 9, 2024 force majeure notice in the factual responses, which are incorporated into the defenses.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Recognizes weakness of 'government action' classification
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer satisfies the criterion. It does not rely on force majeure as the sole defense for Tranches 2/3 and PO-163; it pleads multiple backup defenses, including valid termination for convenience, no anticipatory repudiation, impossibility/commercial impracticability/frustration of purpose, improper tender, failure to mitigate, and seller-remedy limitations. It also acknowledges that the suspension arose from a dispute between Tidewater and Chatham County over change orders, while still asserting force majeure based on events beyond Caldwell’s control and/or government action.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Asserts failure to mitigate damages as affirmative defense
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer does assert a standalone failure-to-mitigate affirmative defense and mentions failure to resell completed goods. However, it does not reference the specific required mitigation fact: that Meridian could have modified/resold the Tranche 2 units or PO-163 components to other buyers for approximately $180,000 in retooling costs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: References Meridian's duty to resell under UCC or common law
criteria_results.reasoning: The failure-to-mitigate defense expressly states that Meridian failed to mitigate under O.C.G.A. § 13-6-5 and the Georgia UCC, including by failing to “resell or attempt to resell completed goods under O.C.G.A. § 11-2-706.” This directly references the seller’s duty to make reasonable resale efforts and provides a statutory legal basis.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Asserts termination for convenience was properly exercised
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly asserts that Caldwell validly exercised its right to terminate for convenience under MSA Section 13.2. It states in paragraph 44 that the November 12, 2024 written notice provided thirty days’ notice with an effective date of December 12, 2024, and the Eighth Defense further pleads valid termination for convenience as an affirmative defense.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Denies force majeure notice constituted repudiation
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly denies that Caldwell’s October 9, 2024 force majeure notice was an anticipatory repudiation, including in response to Paragraph 43 and in the Ninth Defense. It also states that Caldwell reserved and later validly exercised its Section 13.2 termination-for-convenience rights, and denies that any alleged repudiation invalidated that termination.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Limits Caldwell's liability to goods manufactured at time of termination notice
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly asserts multiple times that under MSA § 13.2 Caldwell’s liability after the November 12, 2024 termination notice is limited to conforming goods already manufactured or in the process of manufacture as of that notice date, plus limited documented raw-material costs, and denies liability for the full value of all goods under the POs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Asserts unjust enrichment barred by express contract
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly challenges Count IV by stating in response to Paragraph 86 that the MSA and Purchase Orders are valid, binding, enforceable contracts governing the same subject matter, so no unjust enrichment claim lies under Georgia law. It also repeats this in the Second Defense and Twentieth Defense.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: References Georgia law barring unjust enrichment with express contract
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly states that under Georgia law unjust enrichment is unavailable where valid and enforceable express contracts govern the same subject matter, including in the response to Count IV and in the Second and Twentieth Defenses.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Challenges Meridian's interest calculation of $148,927.80
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer repeatedly denies owing the claimed $148,927.80 interest, challenges Meridian’s calculation as improper and internally inconsistent, states interest applies only to amounts due after acceptance and not to undelivered/unaccepted goods, rejects any acceleration theory, and notes the same figure was claimed for different accrual periods. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Addresses pre-suit negotiation condition precedent
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly addresses MSA Section 15.1 multiple times, specifically denies satisfaction of conditions precedent under Rule 9(c), and asserts a standalone affirmative defense for failure to satisfy pre-suit negotiation requirements. It alleges Meridian did not designate senior representatives, no meeting occurred, Meridian demanded full payment, Caldwell sent one compromise response, and Meridian failed to engage in further good-faith negotiations. Although it does not expressly state that the 30-day waiting period was satisfied, it adequately raises the good-faith negotiation condition precedent issue rather than ignoring it.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Asserts Tranche 2 delivered to wrong location
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly states that the November 15, 2024 attempted Tranche 2 delivery was made to Caldwell's Atlanta offices at 1475 Northside Industrial Boulevard rather than the Project jobsite designated in PO-147, that PO-147 prohibited alternative delivery locations without prior written authorization, that such delivery was non-conforming, and that Caldwell was entitled to refuse it. This is raised in paragraph responses and as an affirmative defense.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Does not adopt Caldwell's incorrect $960,000 figure
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer does not state or admit that Caldwell owes $960,000 for conforming Tranche 1 units. It avoids committing to that figure, treats the January 15 email as a disputed settlement communication, and denies liability for Tranche 1 amounts.

criteria_results.title: Asserts defect rate exceeds AQL
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer repeatedly states that Tranche 1 had 170 defective units out of 800, a 21.25% defect rate, and expressly says this exceeded the MSA’s 2% AQL by more than ten times.

criteria_results.title: Asserts right to reject entire Tranche 1 shipment based on AQL exceedance
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer explicitly asserts that the Tranche 1 shipment had a 21.25% defect rate exceeding the 2% AQL and that MSA Section 4.4 gave Caldwell the right, in its sole discretion, to reject the entire 800-unit shipment, including both defective and non-defective goods. This is stated in the preliminary statement, responses, and Fourth Defense.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Asserts breach of warranty by Meridian
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly raises Meridian’s breach of warranty multiple times, including in the Seventh Defense as a prior material breach of MSA Section 4.3, in the Fifth Defense preserving breach-of-warranty rights under MSA Section 4.3, and in the Eighteenth Defense for setoff/recoupment based on breach of warranty and non-conformity.

criteria_results.title: Handles Ted Caldwell's pre-counsel email with protective measures
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer repeatedly treats Ted Caldwell’s January 15, 2025 email as a settlement/compromise communication under Rule 408, denies that it constitutes any admission of conformity, acceptance, or liability, states any offer was conditional and unaccepted, and avoids adopting any implication that 630 Tranche 1 units were conforming. It therefore includes multiple protective measures required by the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Answer includes Reservations section preserving right to amend
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer includes a separate, substantially equivalent reservation section titled “TWENTY-FOURTH DEFENSE (Reservation of Additional Defenses)” that expressly reserves Caldwell’s right to amend the Answer and assert additional defenses, counterclaims, cross-claims, or third-party claims.

criteria_results.title: Prayer for relief requests dismissal of each count with prejudice
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer includes a prayer for relief requesting dismissal of the action for lack of subject matter jurisdiction and, alternatively, judgment in Caldwell’s favor. However, it does not request dismissal of each count or the Complaint as a whole “with prejudice.”

criteria_results.title: Prayer for relief requests attorneys' fees and costs
criteria_results.reasoning: The prayer for relief expressly requests that Caldwell be awarded its reasonable attorneys' fees, expert witness fees, court costs, and other litigation expenses.

criteria_results.title: Answer does not admit Caldwell 'breached' or 'repudiated' the contract
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer consistently denies allegations that Caldwell breached, repudiated, or anticipatorily breached the MSA or purchase orders. It admits certain facts and contractual obligations, but not an unqualified breach or repudiation; it expressly frames any nonperformance as excused, justified, or subject to contractual rights.

criteria_results.title: DISTRACTOR_002: Does not conflate Irongate purchase with Meridian dispute
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer does not admit or suggest that Caldwell purchased Irongate components as replacements for Meridian’s goods for the Savannah River Project. It expressly denies that any procurement from Irongate has any bearing on Caldwell’s obligations to Meridian, and the remaining references to substitute goods do not identify Irongate or tie it to the Savannah River Project.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies MSA Section 16.1 consequential damages exclusion
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly asserts in the Fifteenth Defense that MSA Section 16.1 bars recovery of indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages, including lost profits and lost revenue.

criteria_results.title: Answer denies Count I (Breach — PO-147 Tranches 2 & 3)
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer specifically addresses Count I (¶¶ 63–69), admits only the existence/enforceability of the MSA and PO-147, and denies the remaining allegations, including the alleged breach, refusal of delivery/payment, and damages. It also asserts defenses regarding force majeure, termination, improper tender, and no obligation to pay for Tranches 2 and 3.

criteria_results.title: Answer denies Count II (Breach — PO-163)
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer specifically addresses Count II (Paragraphs 70–76), admitting only the existence/enforceability of the MSA and PO-163 while denying the alleged breach, refusal/payment liability, damages, and related material allegations, including that Meridian tendered PO-163 goods or completed manufacture.

criteria_results.title: Answer denies Count III (Breach — Tranche 1 unpaid balance)
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly denies Count III’s material allegations, including deemed acceptance and any obligation to pay the $1,280,000 Tranche 1 balance. It asserts that Caldwell timely rejected the Tranche 1 shipment within the inspection period due to nonconformities and repeatedly denies that Tranche 1 was accepted or deemed accepted.

criteria_results.title: Answer denies Count IV (Unjust Enrichment)
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly denies entitlement to unjust enrichment in Count IV, denies that any benefit was conferred or retained, denies the material allegations in paragraphs 86-91, and asserts that the unjust enrichment claim is barred as a matter of law because express contracts govern the subject matter.

criteria_results.title: Affirmative defense: Caldwell's prior material breach / breach by plaintiff
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly asserts a defense titled “Meridian’s Prior Material Breach and Failure to Cure,” alleging Meridian breached by delivering non-conforming Tranche 1 goods and by attempting delivery of Tranche 2 to a prohibited location. It also specifically alleges the 21.25% defect rate exceeding the 2% AQL in another defense.

criteria_results.title: Correctly references MSA Section numbers for key provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer correctly references well over four key MSA provisions by section number, including Sections 4.2/4.3 for specifications and warranties, 5.1 for delivery/FOB Destination, 6.1 for the inspection period, 12.1 for force majeure, 13.2 for termination for convenience, 15.1 for pre-suit negotiation, 16.1 for consequential damages limitations, and 19.1 for notice requirements.

criteria_results.title: Answer addresses the Tranche 1 rejection timeline correctly
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly asserts that Meridian delivered Tranche 1 on September 12, 2024 and that Caldwell sent its written rejection notice on Friday, September 27, 2024, the eleventh business day after delivery and within the 15-business-day Inspection Period under MSA Section 6.1. It repeats this position in the affirmative defenses.

criteria_results.title: Answer correctly references PO numbers
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer identifies CIT-2024-0147 as PO-147 and discusses it as the butterfly-valve purchase order. It identifies CIT-2024-0163 as PO-163 and does not swap it with PO-147 or consistently use an incorrect PO number; while it does not repeatedly describe PO-163 as gate valves, the PO number references are not incorrect or swapped.

criteria_results.title: Force majeure notice timeliness is asserted
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly states that Caldwell sent the force majeure notice on October 9, 2024, after the October 2 suspension notice, and that it was within the ten-business-day period required by MSA Section 12.1. It also reiterates in the force majeure defense that notice was timely.

criteria_results.title: Does not admit full $4,730,400 is owed
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly denies that Caldwell owes Meridian $4,730,400 in the introductory response and elsewhere, and only admits that the combined face value of the purchase orders was $4,730,400 while denying that amount is owed.
